rawFindings.title: read() resolves content incorrectly when encoding is not provided
rawFindings.explanation: In the read() method, the added line `if (!encoding) return resolve(content);` will cause the function to resolve with raw content buffer immediately without applying any escaping (escapeBOM or escapeEOL) when encoding is falsy. This is inconsistent with subsequent behavior that applies escaping when encoding is set, and likely breaks expected output processing.
rawFindings.suggestion: Instead of returning resolve(content) immediately when encoding is falsy, unify the escapeContent processing. Either process the content as string with default encoding before applying escapeContent or handle the raw buffer consistently. For example, remove the early return and always produce a string from content before applying escapeContent if options.escape is true.
